question: Fed Rate Hike by September 2026 Meeting?
resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is increased at any point between December 16, 2025 and the completion of the listed Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting (inclusive of any rate hike announced as a result of the listed meeting). Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

If the listed meeting does not take place within 7 calendar days (ET) of its scheduled end date, 11:59 PM ET, and no qualifying rate hike has been announced, this market will resolve to "No".

Emergency rate hikes will qualify.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the official website of the Federal Reserve (https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm), however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

# Research report 1 of 2

I have enough material and am writing up the brief now. Several search results included material published after 2026-08-26. I left all of it out as instructed. Only items dated on or before 2026-08-26 are used.

## 1. Resolution source
- I tried to fetch the Fed's open market page (federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm) and the July statement. Both requests were refused by the proxy, so I could not read the primary source directly.
- 2026-07-29: The FOMC kept the target range at **3.50%-3.75%**, so the upper bound is 3.75%. That range has been in place since the December 2025 cut. [Fed press release](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20260729a.htm), [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/29/fed-rate-decision-july-2026.html)

## 2. Current status
- 2026-07-29: The hold passed 9-3. Hammack, Kashkari and Logan dissented, all in favour of a 25 bp **hike**. That is the largest dissent since September 2016. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/29/fed-rate-decision-july-2026.html)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- Late August 2026: The Jackson Hole symposium is scheduled for the last week of August. Chair Kevin Warsh's remarks there are widely seen as a key signal.
- 2026-08-19: The July minutes said "Many participants assessed that policy tightening would likely be necessary if inflation did not decline." [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/19/fed-minutes-july-2026-officials-saw-need-for-rate-hike-if-inflation-doesnt-cool.html), [Fed minutes](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomcminutes20260729.htm)
- 2026-08-12/13: July CPI rose 0.1% m/m and 3.4% y/y, down from 3.5% in June. Core CPI rose 0.2% m/m and 2.5% y/y, down from 2.6%. These figures come from secondary reports, not BLS directly, and they disagree on whether the release was August 12 or 13. Reports say traders cut the odds of a September hike afterwards. [KuCoin](https://www.kucoin.com/blog/us-cpi-rises-0-1-in-july-2026-as-expected-core-inflation-eases-to-2-5), [InsiderFinance](https://www.insiderfinance.io/news/july-cpi-2026-eases-while-core-stays-sticky)
- 2026-07-29: Warsh stressed the 2% target. A BMO strategist expected rates to stay on hold at least until September, once the July and August CPI reports are in. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/29/fed-rate-decision-july-2026.html)
- July 2026: June CPI slowed to 3.5% y/y, which pushed back expectations of a hike. [SMM](https://news.metal.com/newscontent/104006513-инфляция-в-сша-в-июне-замедлилась-до-35-отодвигая-ожидания-повышения-ставки-фрс)

## 4. Base rates
- The Fed has not raised rates since July 2023. The cycle since then has been cuts, followed by holds through 2026.
- Three dissents in favour of a hike is unusual. The last time it happened, in September 2016, the Fed did not hike at the next meeting (November 2016) and moved in December 2016. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/29/fed-rate-decision-july-2026.html)
- The Fed rarely hikes when futures price the move below about 50% a few weeks ahead. Usually it signals the move first and pricing ends up near 90% or more by meeting day.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Before the July meeting, markets gave roughly a one-in-three chance of a hike later in 2026. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/29/fed-rate-decision-july-2026.html)
- 2026-08-15: The Kalshi September "hike" contract was reportedly around 26¢. This comes from a secondary summary. [PredictionMarketsPicks](https://predictionmarketspicks.com/articles/fed-rate-hike-odds-september-2026-kalshi-polymarket-futures)
- One report from around the CPI release said futures priced about a 55% chance of a September hold, which implies roughly 45% for a hike. The exact date is unclear. [CryptoBriefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/fed-rate-hike-july-cpi-report/)
- Another report put Polymarket at 53% for a September hike against 32% in futures. I could not confirm its date. [KuCoin](https://www.kucoin.com/news/flash/polymarket-prices-53-odds-of-fed-rate-hike-in-september-2026-vs-32-in-futures)
- Taken together, sources from mid-to-late August put September hike odds at roughly 25-50%, and they disagree with each other. Check the live market before relying on any one number. [Polymarket market](https://polymarket.com/event/fed-decision-in-september-762)

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Late August: Warsh's Jackson Hole speech.
- About August 28: July PCE inflation.
- About September 4: the August jobs report.
- About September 10-11: August CPI. BMO flagged this report as decisive.
- The pre-meeting blackout starts around September 5. After that, Fed officials won't give new guidance.

# Fed rate hike by the September 2026 FOMC meeting: research notes (as of 2026-08-26)

## 1. Resolution source

[Fed press release](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20260729a.htm); [Atlanta Fed](https://www.atlantafed.org/news-and-events/2026/07/29/fomc-statement); [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/29/fed-rate-decision-july-2026.html)
- The range has been 3.50%-3.75% since the late-2025 cuts. I could not find a primary Fed source confirming the exact December 2025 cut date.

## 2. Current status

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-19: The July minutes said many officials thought a rate hike would probably be needed if inflation did not come down. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/19/fed-minutes-july-2026-officials-saw-need-for-rate-hike-if-inflation-doesnt-cool.html)
- 2026-08-12: July CPI came in line with forecasts: headline +0.1% m/m and 3.4% y/y, core +0.2% m/m. Reports say this made a September hike less likely. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/12/cpi-inflation-report-july-2026.html); [Motley Fool](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/12/july-inflation-data-came-in-as-expected-lowering-the-odds-of-a-fed-hike-in-september-yet-again/); [Morningstar](https://www.morningstar.com/economy/middle-road-july-cpi-likely-gives-fed-breathing-room-rate-hikes)
- Early August 2026: July payrolls reportedly fell by 23,000, well below estimates. That weakens the case for tightening. [Motley Fool](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/12/july-inflation-data-came-in-as-expected-lowering-the-odds-of-a-fed-hike-in-september-yet-again/)
- 2026-07-29: The July meeting was Chair Kevin Warsh's first. There were three hawkish dissents, and the 30-year Treasury yield rose above 5.2%, its highest since 2007. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/29/fed-meeting-today-live-updates.html)
- July 2026: Waller said hot core inflation readings would lead the Fed to consider a near-term hike, though he also sees a credible path back to 2% without higher rates. Logan has called for "modestly higher interest rates." Hammack has said some number of hikes may be needed. [Mitrade/Motley Fool](https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-8-1916977-20260720); [Newsquawk](https://www.newsquawk.com/headlines/primer---todays-fedspeak-includes-waller-hammack-goolsbee)
- Oil prices and Iran/Strait of Hormuz developments are cited as a key swing factor for inflation.

## 4. Base rates
- Since late 2025 the Fed has made no hikes. It held at every 2026 meeting through July: January (10-2, with two dovish dissents), March, April, June (12-0) and July (9-3, with three hawkish dissents). [Chatham](https://www.chathamfinancial.com/insights/fomc-recap-1-28-26); [Advisor Perspectives](https://advisorperspectives.com/dshort/updates/2026/06/18/feds-interest-rate-decision-june-17-2026)
- Three dissents in favor of a hike is unusual, and the Fed has historically often moved soon after a cluster of dissents. But under Powell and earlier chairs, the Fed rarely made its first hike of a cycle without first signaling it clearly.
- The Fed has not used an emergency intermeeting hike since the early 1990s. Emergency moves in recent decades have been cuts (2001, 2008, 2020).

## 5. Other forecasts
- 2026-08-12: CME FedWatch put the chance of a September hike at about 38%, down from about 48% the day before, with a hold at about 62%. Another source put the hike odds at 42%. The chance of a hike by December was about 45%. [Motley Fool](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/12/july-inflation-data-came-in-as-expected-lowering-the-odds-of-a-fed-hike-in-september-yet-again/); [BigGo](https://finance.biggo.com/news/575a7c94-fb73-4088-86dc-8bc15c88214b)
- After the July CPI report, Bank of America scaled back its call for three hikes by year-end.
- After the July meeting, futures were pricing two hikes, in September and December. [AgWest](https://www.agwestfc.com/education-and-resources/industry-and-economic-insights/economic-updates/updates-from-the-fed/fomc-meeting-results)
- I could not find a Polymarket or Kalshi price for the September hike with a verifiable date between 2026-08-20 and 2026-08-26. In mid-to-late August, market pricing for a September hike looked to be in roughly the 25-40% range, but I could not pin down an exact figure as of 08-26.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Late August 2026: The Jackson Hole symposium, with a keynote by Chair Warsh. This is the main near-term signal for September, and markets are expected to react strongly to whatever he says about hikes. [Yahoo Finance live page](https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/live/jackson-hole-fed-summit-live-kevin-warsh-keynote-speech-180442096.html)
- Late August 2026: July PCE inflation data.
- Early September 2026: The August jobs report. Another negative payroll print would argue against a hike.
- Mid-September 2026: August CPI and PPI, released shortly before the meeting.
- From about 2026-09-05: The pre-meeting blackout period starts, with no more Fed speeches.

- Yes: Warsh signals at Jackson Hole that tightening is warranted given oil-driven headline inflation and unanchoring risk. August CPI comes in hot, at 0.4% or more on core. Markets move to above 80% and the Fed hikes 25bp.

However, core inflation at 2.5% and negative payrolls make a hike in September hard to justify. The decisive data, Jackson Hole and August CPI, are still unknown, which keeps meaningful uncertainty. I settle slightly below the market, at about 22%.

(f) **From base rate to final number.** I start from market pricing of roughly 26-38% in mid-August. I shade down because:
- the data since then (benign core inflation, negative payrolls) points against a hike;
- the Fed rarely surprises with a first hike of a cycle that is not fully priced;
- the 2016 precedent suggests dissent clusters do not force an immediate move.

Some hawkish tail risk remains, from the minutes and the dissenters. I land around 18%.
